title: Half the NQ strategies that look profitable since 2023 are just long the Nasdaq with extra steps
author: person-person12
selftext:
The hardest thing to tell about your own strategy isnt whether it made money, its whether it made money **for a reason other than NQ going up**. Since mid 2023 the index has mostly climbed, so a lot of long biased setups look like they have an edge when theyre really just holding the trend for a few minutes at a time.

I found this out on the Powell 10am setup everybody was posting about. I coded it and replayed it on 1m NQ candles from july 2023 to feb 2026, 1 contract, 535 trades. Overall it finished at a 0.98 profit factor and net -$3,675, which is already a no, but the split by market conditions is the part worth seeing.

**The only stretch where it made money was uptrends**, 152 trades at a 1.08 profit factor for +$3,307. The 280 trades taken in volatile conditions lost $6,764 at a 0.93 profit factor. Buy and hold over the same window took 100k to about 170k while the strategy did -3.7% on the same account.

So the little bit of edge it showed came from the same place buy and hold got its 70%, and the setup itself was paying spread and slippage to rent it in small pieces. If I had only looked at the uptrend months I would have called it a working strategy.

Now every time I run something in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) I split the trades by regime and put buy and hold next to it before I look at net profit. A setup that only pays in the conditions where just holding the index paid more hasnt shown me anything yet, and most of the ones I test land there.
